subject: Post-demo: sample query capture + eval recommendations (BrightLedger)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightledger.com>; Priya Rao <priya.r@brightledger.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-03T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: sample query capture + eval recommendations (BrightLedger)

Thanks again for the demo time earlier today — felt like a productive session. Quick written recap and a narrow ask so we can kick off a lightweight eval that maps to the workflows you showed: invoice question answering, vendor reconciliation, and customer support triage. Attached: post-demo-notes.pdf (call highlights + meeting recording link).

What we need from you to get an actionable eval: (goal: a minimal prompt set that captures expected query distribution and edge cases)
- 200–300 representative customer queries (CSV is fine). Include the original user text and the desired output/label where possible.
- Flag ~20 edge cases explicitly (short note per row) — examples: nested instructions, invoice-like text with masked account numbers, multilingual phrases, intentionally ambiguous requests.
- Mark anything that cannot leave your environment (PII / account numbers) — we will provide a redaction checklist and options for local-only handling.

Suggested timeline: if you can drop the CSV by end-of-week (Fri, 9/05), we’ll turn around an initial model-fit report and sample eval within 5 business days.

Internally, I’ve looped in Connor (CS) and Neha (solutions) to:
- Connor: help with ingestion templates and any API toggles for conservative tokenization/batching.
- Neha: will own redaction guidance and quick data quality checks.

Next steps (for clarity):
1) Sam / Priya: share sample queries CSV + callouts (deadline: 2025-09-05 EOD)
2) Redwood: baseline run on 2 candidate models, produce accuracy/latency table + suggested quantization profile
3) Joint sync after initial report to agree on production pilot scope

Thanks — happy to hop back on a short call if you want to walk through the CSV format.

— Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(attachment: post-demo-notes.pdf)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightledger.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.r@brightledger.com>
Date: 2025-09-03T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sample query capture + eval recommendations (BrightLedger)

Avery — thanks, appreciate the clear ask. Attaching an initial dump: customer-examples.csv (flagged few rows for internal-only). A few quick clarifications inline below: 

- We can provide ~250 rows that reflect a mix: 60% support Q&A, 25% invoice/vendor reconciliation, 15% misc/tricky edge cases.
- Edge cases we’ll tag with column EDGE_FLAG and a short note. Examples we included:
  * "What's the invoice total after refund?" (requires arithmetic + state)
  * "We need to split payment between vendor A and B — show allocation" (multi-step)
  * partially masked account numbers like XXXX-XXXX-1234 that we would prefer redacted before sharing
- For PII: we will remove full names and SSN-like strings before upload; account numbers we can mask but want to flag so you know they exist in production flows.

Attachment: customer-examples.csv (CSV, 250 rows) — I’ve put a small sample in the email body below for formatting guidance. If you need a different schema, let us know quickly.

Sample rows (first 3):
1,"Invoice 3921 shows incorrect tax. Can you confirm?","Support / Invoice","desired: 'Tax discrepancy — send corrected invoice'","EDGE_FLAG:"
2,"Split this vendor payment 60/40 for Acme Supplies","Reconciliation","desired: 'Allocate amounts and generate transfer lines'","EDGE_FLAG: multi-step"
3,"Tengo un problema con mi factura, ¿cómo se resuelve?","Support (es)","desired: 'Provide steps in Spanish'","EDGE_FLAG: multilingual"

We’ll share the full CSV via a secure link to your shared Drive folder by EOD Friday. Happy to redact more aggressively if required — please send your redaction checklist.

Best,
Sam
Head of Product | BrightLedger
(attachment: customer-examples.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>; Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightledger.com>, Priya Rao <priya.r@brightledger.com>
Date: 2025-09-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sample query capture + eval recommendations (BrightLedger)

Looping in model/eval recommendations and a suggested redaction checklist. Thanks Sam for the sample preview — looks good. High-level plan from eval team (quick):

Model candidates to baseline (fast turn):
- rw-instruct-7b-v2 (server-friendly, strong instruction following)
- rw-serve-13b-ptq (higher throughput; use 4-bit PTQ for cost/latency tradeoff)

Planned metrics we’ll report: exact-match / F1 (for extraction tasks), instruction-completion accuracy, latency p95 (per request), and a simple hallucination rate estimate on a held-out prompt subset.

Redaction checklist (we will formalize this as a short doc):
- Remove or mask: full names, SSNs, payment card numbers (PAN), full account numbers. Replace with [NAME] / [SSN] / [PAN] / [ACCOUNT] tokens.
- For partially-masked account numbers (e.g., XXXX-1234), keep the masking but note the mask format in an EDGE_FLAG column.
- Keep language indicators (lang: es/en) in a LANG column so we can evaluate multilingual behavior.
- For any rows with legal text / contracts: include a HIGH_SENSITIVITY flag — we will run those through a private-only ingest path and not store them in long-term eval corpora.

Data ingestion notes for Connor:
- Use sample-prompts.csv template (attached) with columns: id, raw_text, desired_response, lang, edge_flag, sensitivity_tag.
- If BrightLedger prefers S3 or one-time secure upload instead of Drive, we can accept a presigned link.

Benchmarks & reference: I’ve started a shared folder and seeded with our lightweight benchmark harness and a small synthetic set for invoice extraction: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cBenchmarkSamples. Also added a draft eval checklist at https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/brightledger/2025-eval-report (view-only).

Connor/Neha — can you confirm the ingestion schema and any special handling for the HIGH_SENSITIVITY flagged rows? We should also confirm whether BrightLedger wants evaluation results in .csv or a short slide pack.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: sample-prompts.csv)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightledger.com>, Priya Rao <priya.r@brightledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-05T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sample query capture + eval recommendations (BrightLedger)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sam. Confirming next steps and an action matrix so responsibilities/timing are explicit: 

Action matrix (concise)
- BrightLedger (Sam/Priya): deliver full customer-examples.csv with EDGE_FLAG + LANG + sensitivity_tag columns (due 2025-09-05 EOD). If you want us to redact account numbers first, indicate REDACT_BEFORE_UPLOAD.
- Redwood (Marissa/Connor/Neha): ingest and run baseline on rw-instruct-7b-v2 and rw-serve-13b-ptq; deliver a short eval report (csv + 1-slide exec summary) within 5 business days after we receive CSV.
- Joint: sync to review pilot scope (30–60 minute call) within 2 business days of the report.

Quick notes on priorities for the CSV: prioritize real user phrasing and include negative examples where the user intent is unclear — those are often where models regress. When flagging edge cases, a one-line note is enough (e.g., "requires arithmetic", "currency conversion", "sensitive contract clause").

Redaction preferences: our standard approach is to accept masked account numbers (XXXX-1234) and a sensitivity tag. If you choose to mask before upload, please keep the mask consistent across rows. We will not try to deanonymize masked tokens. For HIGH_SENSITIVITY rows, we will run inference in a private-only path and not retain training artifacts.

Deliverables once we complete the baseline:
- Model-fit table (accuracy / latency / cost per 1k tokens)
- Suggested production profile (batching, quantization level, caching policy)
- Short regression guardrails: prompt templates + test prompts to run on future model updates

If that all sounds good, Sam — please confirm that EOD Fri works for you. I’ll schedule a quick 20-minute sync for Tue 9/09 after the report unless you prefer earlier.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

— Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
(attachment: sample-prompts.csv)
